blocks.raw: <Tip>Hypocenter and epicenter are like a lightbulb (hypocenter) and the shadow it casts on the ceiling (epicenter). The bulb releases the energy; the shadow shows where to look up.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing epicenter with hypocenter. The epicenter is on the surface; the hypocenter is the rupture point at depth.","Treating magnitude and intensity as equivleant. Magnitude measures energy; intensity measures perception and damage. One earthquake, one magnitude, many intensities.","Using Richter sclea (ML) for large events. Richter saturates above ML 6.5. Use moment magnitude (Mw) for M 7+.","Calculating intensity from a formula. Intensity is assigned by observation of damage, not derived from a calculation.","Confusing epicentral distance with depth. Distance from epicenter ≠ hypocenter depth. Both affect ground motion but are independent."]} />
